title: POC data contracts and ingest playbook
summary: Working playbook for onboarding customer data into a POC: defines data contract, minimal ingestion pipeline, validation checks, roles, timeline, and workshop agenda. Focused on mitigating downstream model quality and compliance risks.
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical runbook for solutions engineering and the customer's data team to get a POC from zero to ingesting validated example traffic into Redwood’s hosted/dedicated runtime. Primary goals: define a small, testable data contract, implement a reproducible ingest path, and verify behavioral regression/quality checks before scaling to production traffic.

Scope and constraints:
- Target POC: chat/assist feature + retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for a single internal dataset (customer documents).
- Ingest window: up to 50K docs (or 5GB), initially only metadata + text fields. No binary blobs in phase 1.
- Compliance: PII scanning required; customer provides KMS key for encrypted transfers if requested.
- We accept data in either S3 or secure FTP. S3 preferred.

Quick timeline (two-week sprint):
- Day -7: Data readiness call (customer), share sample schema and example payloads. Assign roles.
- Day 0: Kickoff workshop (2h) — alignment on contract + minimal transformation rules.
- Day 1–3: Customer drops sample data (<= 100 docs). SE runs quick ingest script and returns validation report.
- Day 4–7: Implement ingest adapter, lightweight ETL (normalize dates, strip markup, enforce length).
- Day 8: Internal demo with basic prompts, capture output.
- Day 9–10: Fix pitfalls (tokenization surprises, noise), run evaluation prompts + quality checklist.
- Day 11: Prep handoff doc for operations & optional canary plan.
- Day 12–14: Run fallback and failure scenario tests; sign off POC acceptance criteria.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Solutions Engineer (owner): Marisol Reyes — runs ingest adapter, validation harness, demo prompts, coordinates with customer.
content_line_2:
- Customer Data Lead: provides sample exports, answers schema questions, swaps in KMS if needed.
- Security/Compliance SME: Priya Nair — approves PII redaction strategy and retention settings.
- Infra/Platform Contact: Samir Khan — configures S3 access, network rules for dedicated/private POC.

Minimal data contract (phase 1) — keys and expectations:
- id: string (stable, customer-provided)
- source: string (document origin like 'hr-handbook', 'table-of-contents')
- created_at: RFC3339 timestamp (best-effort)
- title: short string (optional)
- body_text: plain text UTF-8 (required, <= 100k chars)
- language: ISO-639-1 (optional, default 'en')
- metadata: flat key:value map (limited to 20 keys for POC)
Notes: any HTML or markdown should be transformed to text; binaries must be separated out and referenced by URL only.

Acceptance criteria (must be met for POC sign-off):
- Ingest pipeline accepts sample schema without errors for >=95% of documents.
- Automated PII scanner reports no high-risk PII in the supplied test set (or customer approves redaction decisions).
- Baseline prompt suite yields non-empty, syntactically reasonable responses for 90% of test prompts.
- No tokenization explosions (>3x expected token count) on more than 1% of docs.
- End-to-end demo (customer prompt -> Redwood response) completes within P99 latency SLO for the chosen config.

Validation checklist (automated + manual):
1) Schema conformance check (script): presence/format of id, body_text, language.
2) Character encoding scan: flag non-UTF8 sequences.
3) Fragmentation/dup detection: simple hash-based dedupe of title+body_text.
4) Tokenization sanity: report mean, 90th, 99th token counts per doc (tokenizer = model-specific).
5) PII scan: run regex + model-assisted classifier; output redaction suggestions as a CSV.
6) Small-sample QA: SE crafts 10 exemplar prompts that should pass/fail; capture expected output.

Ingest pipeline (minimal reference):
- Step A: Customer uploads sample to agreed S3 prefix (s3://cust-alpha/poc/samples/).
- Step B: SE runs ingest-adapter (python script) with flags: --sample --dry-run. Produces validation report and normalized JSONL.
- Step C: Push normalized JSONL to staging index (vector db or Redwood storage) behind feature flag.
- Step D: Run evaluation prompt suite (workbook attached) and produce pass/fail results.
- Step E: If pass, push to canary route for live testing with traffic shadow.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Unexpected markup/embedded HTML -> add html-to-text step; capture sample and ask customer to sanitize at source.
- Extremely long docs -> chunking policy: 4k token sliding windows with 512 overlap (configurable).
- Non-UTF8 or legacy encodings -> transcode and report back to customer.
- PII discovered late -> holdback dataset; propose redaction/field-masking; update contract for retention limits.

Workshop agenda (2h):
- 0:00–0:10 Introductions, success definition (who signs off).
- 0:10–0:30 Review sample data and live walkthrough of a single doc.
- 0:30–0:55 Align on data contract: required fields, retention, redaction rules.
- 0:55–1:20 Ingestion demo: run adaptor on a sample and review validation output.
- 1:20–1:45 Risk heatmap: performance, tokenization, PII, quota. Decide immediate mitigations.
- 1:45–2:00 Next steps, ownership, and calendar of small deliverables.

Decision log (examples):
- 2026-01-20: Agreed to accept S3 only for phase 1 (Marisol, CustomerDataLead) — reason: simplifies transfer and permissions.
- 2026-01-22: Chunking policy set to 4k tokens with 512 overlap (Priya) — reason: balance context vs cost.
- 2026-02-02: Use customer-managed KMS for encrypted transfers (Samir) — reason: compliance request.

Communication templates (short snippets):
- "Can you upload 50 representative files to s3://cust-alpha/poc/samples/ by EOD Wednesday? We'll run the adapter and share the validation report."
- "Validation report attached — key issues: 12 docs with non-UTF8 chars, 3 docs flagged for probable SSN patterns. Please confirm redaction strategy."

Handoff & ops notes:
- If POC passes, create a runbook for ops with: S3 prefix, retention policy, index names, model variants tested, quantization profile (if any), and autoscaling targets for dedicated capacity.
- Tag all artifacts in GitHub and Confluence with the POC id (use JIRA key SE-8721).

Open questions / To do before kickoff:
- Customer: can you provide an example export with at least one document that contains complex markup? (yes/no)
- SE: prepare truncated tokenizer metrics script and attach to repo.
- Security: confirm whether the PII classifier output must be retained or can be ephemeral.

Appendix: sample minimal JSONL line (single-line example)
{"id": "doc-1234", "source": "policy-handbook", "created_at": "2024-11-06T12:22:44Z", "title": "Return policy", "body_text": "Employees must return assets to IT when leaving...", "language": "en", "metadata": {"department": "ops", "sensitivity": "internal"}}

-- end of playbook --
Notes to self: keep this light for initial teams; if customer asks for richer attachments, spin a separate "binary handling" mini-POC.
